result.summary: The street environment is narrow and lacks dedicated pedestrian infrastructure on both sides. Pedestrians are forced to share the roadway with vehicles due to the absence of a defined sidewalk on the right and a very narrow, unbuffered walkway on the left.

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk continuity
hazards.description: There is no sidewalk on the right side of the street, forcing pedestrians to walk in the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street adjacent to the grey building

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right side block sightlines between pedestrians and moving traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a raised, ADA-compliant sidewalk on the right side of the street to provide a safe, dedicated walking space.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or a shared street (woonerf) design to slow vehicle speeds in this narrow corridor.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained concrete sidewalk in a residential area with modern buildings. While the walkway is clear and in good condition, there is no physical buffer between pedestrians and the roadway, and no street-level lighting or trees are visible along the curb.

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the travel lane, increasing exposure to moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground

hazards.name: Degraded roadway surface
hazards.description: The asphalt surface appears worn and uneven, which can affect vehicle control and create tripping hazards if pedestrians cross mid-block.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce a planting zone between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during evening hours.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by incomplete infrastructure, with a sidewalk present only on one side of the street and no buffer from traffic. While the upcoming intersection features a marked crosswalk and stop control, the lack of a continuous walkway on the left and narrow paths on the right create a less-than-ideal environment for walking.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a formal sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway or navigate between parked cars.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street adjacent to the grey building

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the left curb block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.

interventions.title: New Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility by preventing parking near the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Add a planting strip with street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a standard-width concrete sidewalk separated from a large fenced lot by a chain-link fence. The area lacks street lighting, shade trees, and any buffer between the walkway and the roadway, creating a barren and exposed environment.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Cracking
hazards.description: Visible cracks and uneven joints in the concrete sidewalk panels create minor tripping hazards.

hazards.name: Lack of Street Lighting
hazards.description: No street light poles are visible, which significantly reduces pedestrian safety and security after dark.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The long stretch of chain-link fence and open lot provides no 'eyes on the street', reducing perceived safety.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and center background along the sidewalk edge

interventions.title: Street Lighting Installation
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and security at night.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add a planting strip with street trees between the curb and sidewalk to provide a physical buffer from traffic and improve the microclimate.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Patch or replace cracked concrete panels to ensure a smooth, ADA-compliant walking surface.
